title: 中文書名:微流體環境中的智能機器人定位極限 MICROFLUIDIC ENVIRONMENT IN INTELLIGENT ROBOT LOCALIZATION AT THE LIMIT This 777-page English research monograph asks whether intelligent robot localization in microfluidic environments can improve sample-identity probability without increasing contact impulse or carryover. The book contains 30 mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 single-page studies, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. It covers microfluidic flow, optical and multimodal localization, state estimation, data association, closed-loop control, sample identity, uncertainty, blinded fault tests and independent reconstruction. The work is nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim completed clinical testing, proven in-body efficacy or autonomous medical authority. Identity, contact, carryover, purity, calibration and external reconstruction must pass together.
